direction: 15m long-only spot mean-reversion after large negative candle, with full rebound target and maximum holding timeout
economic_falsification: Recent primary-source evidence estimates roughly 1.3bp gross reversal edge versus 5bp benchmark round-trip costs. The repository cost model is materially higher (10bp fee per side before spread/slippage/impact); keep the actual costly simulation to measure the specific full-rebound rule and turnover, with no expectation of profitability.
hypothesis: Some large short-horizon selloffs may mean-revert before a fixed short holding cap. Longer holding caps can capture rebounds but increase exposure to continuing declines; larger entry shocks reduce frequency. Costs are likely to dominate at the repository fee assumption, making this a falsification-oriented historical test.
rule: At completed UTC 15m signal bar j, compute r=C[j]/C[j-1]-1. If flat and r<=-entry_drop_fraction, buy long on the next 15m block at block_start+60s; record C[j] as the recovery reference and the 15m bar index of execution. While long, use only completed 15m closes: exit when C[j]>=recovery_reference, or when j-entry_execution_bar_index>=max_holding_15m_bars, whichever occurs first. Exit at next block_start+60s. After any exit, no same-bar re-entry; later completed bars may generate new entries. Signals use closes only, do not peek into the following bar, and the exit cap is a hard time stop rather than a price stop. Cash/units persist; no leverage, short, scale-in, interest, or OOS warm-up trades.
allocation: Each asset/parameter definition is a separate 2,000 USDT long-only spot account with at most one position; no transfer or simultaneous cross-asset position.

failure_gates.interpretation: A pass would be only a repeated-history screen; it is not independent OOS or live-profit evidence.

literature.citation: Kitron, N.A. & Wengrowicz, J.M. (2026). Short-horizon mean reversion in cryptocurrency markets: a matched cross-market measurement. arXiv:2608.21888, version accessed 2026-10-12.
literature.use: The authors report 15-minute directional mean reversion across Binance crypto pairs, but estimate only about 1.3 bp gross edge per trade against a 5 bp benchmark round-trip cost. This fixed one-coin shock/rebound rule is a predeclared implementation test, not a replication; it adds longer rebound targets, own-account execution costs and tail risk.

data.source: Binance spot closed 1m OHLCV aggregated into UTC 15m bars
data.reuse_disclosure: The full period is repeatedly used development/validation history; not an untouched final holdout.

walk_forward.parameter_fit: None; rules and grid frozen before results. Previous closed bars warm only signal/cost inputs; OOS account starts with cash and carries position across contiguous test folds.

execution.reference_price: On signal close availability at each UTC 15m boundary, execute on the following 15m block first 1m open after one-minute buffer (block_start+60s). Rebound/timeout liquidation follows the same delay. No historical L2 quotes; actual historical 1m OHLCV opens are only reference prices, not exchange fills.

costs.impact_formula: 0.5 * sample std(previous 20 completed UTC daily log returns) * sqrt(order budget / mean quote turnover(previous 20 complete UTC days)

prior_evidence.finding: All 16 original rows already have actual backtest evidence; this is a new 15m configuration family, not an attempt to relabel old results.
